newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures ease late, end mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures ease late, end mixed.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mixed after a choppy afternoon in which December S&P 500s rose to new all-time highs and then slipped to end lower on the day.
Some linked the decline in the final 45 minutes of the session to weakness in key technology stocks.
"The turnaround in Microsoft really put the kibosh on our rally," said Kevin O'Brien, stock index futures analyst on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange at Prudential Securities.

In addition, O'Brien said the inability of the market to maintain gains in the face of strength in Nasdaq stocks created wariness of the advance, which also prompted selling in index futures late in the day.

Earlier in the afternoon, strength in the bond market initiated buying in index futures that sent the December S&P 500 contract to a new all-time high, above the prior high set overnight during GLOBEX dealings.
The advance triggered a few light arbitrage buy programs, which traders said occurred when the December S&P premium over the spot widened above about 3.25 points.
The nearby S&P contract managed to stay above intraday support traders cited near 745.00 during the late fall, which some viewed as a positive sign.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures ended firm but in the lower portion of daily ranges after also coming under pressure late.

At settlement, December S&P 500s were off 0.15 point at 746.15, Russell 2000s gained 1.20 point to 349.60, Value Line futures were up 0.95 point to 673.25, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 135.0 to 21,160.0 and Midcap 400s gained 0.55 point to 254.40. --Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750/email:derivatives@reuters.com
